name: CA-36
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of about 21 points on partisan vote index
Incumbent Ted Lieu running with a large financial advantage over a minimally funded challenger
Prediction markets price Lieu near certain to win
No general-election polling, but fundamentals leave little doubt
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Lieu: a +21 Democratic district, incumbency, and a roughly 350-to-1 fundraising edge over Houston Brignano, who has raised only about $5,000. Markets price Lieu at 97 percent, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Only a major late scandal or an unexpected collapse in Democratic turnout across California could narrow this margin meaningfully.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ted Lieu seeks another term in a Los Angeles-area district that leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan vote index of about +21 for his party. He is a well-established incumbent who has held the seat comfortably for years.

His challenger, Republican Houston Brignano, has raised only about $5,000 and reports under $1,000 on hand, while Lieu has raised more than $1.8 million and holds over $1.1 million in cash. Outside spending is minimal on both sides. No general-election polls are available, but prediction markets put Lieu's chances near 97 percent. With no expert ratings and no polling to complicate the picture, the race rests on fundamentals that all point the same direction: a safe Democratic hold with a margin in the mid-20s.
